facts.statement: Bolong is a genus of iguanodontian dinosaur found in the Early Cretaceous Yixian Formation of western Liaoning Province, China.
facts.quote: Bolong (meaning "Bo's dragon") is a genus of iguanodontian dinosaur known from the Early Cretaceous Yixian Formation of western Liaoning Province, China.

facts.statement: Bolong lived approximately 125 million years ago during the earliest Barremian stage.
facts.quote: It lived about 125 million years ago in the earliest Barremian.

facts.statement: The genus Bolong was named by Wu Wen-hao, Pascal Godefroit, and Hu Dong-yu in 2010.
facts.quote: It was named by Wu Wen-hao, Pascal Godefroit and Hu Dong-yu in 2010.

facts.statement: The genus name Bolong honors the brothers Bo Hai-chen and Bo Xue, who assisted in its discovery, and the Chinese word for dragon.
facts.quote: The genus name is derived from the names of the brothers Bo Hai-chen and Bo Xue, who helped uncover it, and the Mandarin word 龍 lóng "dragon".

facts.statement: The holotype specimen, YHZ-001, is a nearly complete skeleton.
facts.quote: The holotype fossil, YHZ-001, consists of a nearly complete skeleton.

facts.statement: A second specimen, ZMNH-M8812, an almost complete skeleton of a juvenile, was found by a farmer near Xitaizhi in Inner Mongolia in 2013.
facts.quote: In 2013 a second specimen (ZMNH-M8812) was described consisting of an almost complete skeleton of a very young animal. It was found by a farmer near the village of Xitaizhi in Inner Mongolia.

facts.statement: Bolong was a relatively small dinosaur with an estimated length of 4 meters and a weight of 200 kilograms.
facts.quote: Bolong was a relatively small animal with an estimated length of 4 m and a weight of 200 kg.

facts.statement: Bolong had a convex, stocky head with powerful mandibles and relatively large teeth.
facts.quote: The head is convex and fairly stocky with powerful mandibles. The teeth are relatively large.

facts.statement: The gait of Bolong is debated; its short forelimbs with unfused wrist bones suggest they were not well-adapted for weight-bearing, despite proportions reminiscent of quadrupeds.
facts.quote: The gait of Bolong is disputed. The forelimb was fairly short, and the wrist bones were not fused together, suggesting that the forelimb was not well-adapted to bearing much weight, though the proportions of the distal forelimb are reminiscent of quadrupeds.

facts.statement: Bolong's short and robust hind foot resembles that of fully quadrupedal dinosaurs rather than bipedal ones.
facts.quote: However, the hind foot was short and robust, more like fully quadrupedal dinosaurs than bipedal ones.

facts.statement: Very young Bolong individuals had proportionally longer forelimbs, typical of quadrupedal animals.
facts.quote: Very young individuals had a proportionally longer forelimb, typical of the proportions of quadrupedal animals.

facts.statement: Bolong is classified within Hadrosauroidea and is considered one of the most basal hadrosauroids found in Asia.
facts.quote: The describers placed Bolong in Hadrosauroidea. It would have been one of the basalmost hadrosauroids found in Asia.

facts.statement: Bolong belongs to the family Iguanodontidae.
Bolong is a member of the class Ornithischia.
Bolong lived from the Barremian to the Aptian stages, between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Aptian (125.77 to 119.57 million years ago)

rejected.statement: Researchers suggest Bolong was a facultative quadruped that spent much of its time walking bipedally, based on thigh and shin proportions.
rejected.quote: This suggests that Bolong was a facultative quadruped that spent much of its time walking bipedally, which is also suggested by the relative proportions of the thigh and shin.
